messages:
anna: Quick heads-up — ran an nsys trace on a prod-like run (bsz=4, seq=2048, KV cache enabled) to investigate yesterday's perf regression. Seeing periodic 10–25ms stalls. nvtx timeline points to memory-bank-conflict-ish behavior during the fused attention + KV write window.

perf-bot: nsys upload: https://perf.company/trace/1805004321 (full timeline + counters)

kevin: which kernels are spiking? can you paste the timeline snippet?

anna: here's the hot slice from the timeline (trimmed):
```text
[  12.3ms] flash_attn_fwd_kernel      0.9ms
[  23.1ms] fused_attn_kv_write        15.8ms   <-- long stall window
[  39.0ms] sgemm_128x128              1.1ms
```

devon: fused_attn_kv_write that high is surprising. Looks like write path is blocking compute. Could be bank conflicts or uncoalesced stores. Also check if tensor-core fallbacks are triggered (small tiles).

sam: any host-side syncs or logging inside the loop? those can look like GPU stalls but are actually sync points.

anna: double-checked — no host syncs in the hot path. I pulled low-level counters: high L2 write traffic and increased `lts__t_sectors_pipe_lsu_mem_global_op_st.sum`. Bank-conflict-ish metric (custom heuristic) ~1.6x baseline.

kevin: interesting. try running a microbench that writes KV in the same layout to confirm bank conflict vs overall memory saturation. also compare with `flash_variant=alt` or disable fused path to see delta.

devon: suggestion: pad the head_dim or change KV layout (split heads into 2 blocks) to avoid aliasing on the same memory banks. Alternatively try chunked/double-buffer writes to reduce simultaneous bank pressure.

anna: I tried the alt flash variant and the results look promising: fused_attn_kv_write drops from 15.8ms -> 3.2ms, but overall fwd attn runtime increases ~10% because we add an extra memcpy and more register pressure. Uploaded alt trace: https://perf.company/trace/1805004321/alt

kevin: that suggests the alt variant avoids the pathological bank alignment but at cost of extra memory ops. For a quick mitigation we could route seq>1024 to the alt variant in the kernel-selector heuristic. Long-term we should optimize the write loop (use wider stores or change stride).

sam: I'll craft a small reproducer kernel that models the KV write stride and run it with nsys+nvprof counters for bank_conflict, L2 requests, and DRAM BW to isolate whether it's conflict vs saturation.

devon: also add a unit/regression check in the perf harness that measures KV write p99 for a set of seq lengths and head dims so we catch future regressions.

anna: plan: open an issue with trace links, add a quick heuristic fallback (alt variant) for >1024 seq, and follow up with microbench + kernel rewrite PR. I'll post the issue/PR once I have the microbench results.

kevin: sgtm. thanks for the trace and the alt test — really helpful.

anna: :thumbsup: will update thread with PR link.
